habitat.hostAssociation: Normal gut colonizer in a minority of healthy adults; overgrows when normal flora is disrupted by antibiotics
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Hardy spores persist for long periods on hospital surfaces

culture.media: Cycloserine-cefoxitin fructose agar (CCFA), taurocholate-based selective media
culture.colonyMorphology: Flat, gray-yellow colonies with a ground-glass texture; characteristic "horse-manure" odor
culture.pigmentation: Yellowish under UV fluorescence on CCFA

identificationClues: Toxin A/B detection (EIA or PCR) confirms toxigenic infection, not culture alone
Pseudomembranes seen on colonoscopy in severe colitis

virulenceFactors: Toxin B (cytotoxin) — the primary driver of colitis
Hypervirulent strains (e.g. ribotype 027) produce a binary toxin and more toxin A/B
clinicalImportance.transmission: Fecal-oral via spores, which are resistant to alcohol-based hand sanitizer and many disinfectants; healthcare-associated transmission is common
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: Leading cause of healthcare-associated diarrhea; strongly associated with prior broad-spectrum antibiotic use (e.g. clindamycin, fluoroquinolones, cephalosporins)
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Diagnosis relies on toxin detection (EIA/NAAT) rather than culture alone, since asymptomatic colonization with non-toxigenic strains is common

examFacts.importantTest: Stool toxin EIA or nucleic acid amplification test
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Disease requires toxin production, not merely colonization — spores resist alcohol-based hand sanitizer
